identity.author: Acts of the Martyrs
identity.edition: Gebhardt, Acta martyrum selecta (1902), Passio SS. Mariani et Iacobi

sections.locus: Gebhardt XIII.I (preface; Marianus and James named)
source_text: Quotiens aliquid beatissimi martyres dei omnipotentis et Christi eius festinantes ad promissa regna caelorum carissimis suis uerecundius mandant, memores humilitatis quae semper in fide solet facere maiores, quanto modestius petiuerunt, tanto efficacius impetrauerunt. Et nobis quoque hoc praedicandae gloriae suae munus dei testes nobilissimi reliquerunt, Marianum dico, ex dilectissimis fratribus nostris, et Iacobum, quos mihi scitis praeter communem sacramenti religionem, uitae etiam societate et domesticis affectibus inhaesisse. Qui contra saeuientis saeculi pressuras et gentiles impetus habituri tam sublime certamen, praelium suum, quod instinctu spiritus caelestis inierunt, in notitiam fraternitatis per nos uenire iusserunt, non quod in terris uellent coronae suae gloriam per iactantiam praedicari, sed ut praecedentibus experimentis multitudo plebis et dei populus ad exemplum fidei posset armari. Nec inmerito id obsecuturo mihi fiducia familiaris iniunxit. Quis enim dubitet quae nobis in pace uitae communitas fuerit, quando nos indiuidua dilectione uiuentes unum tempus persecutionis inuenerit?
english: Whenever the most blessed martyrs of almighty God and of his Christ, hastening toward the promised kingdom of heaven, lay some charge upon their dearest friends with a becoming modesty, remembering the humility that in faith always makes men greater, the more modestly they asked, the more powerfully they prevailed. To me also, in the same way, those most noble witnesses of God have left this office of declaring their glory, I mean Marianus, one of our dearest brothers, and James, who, as you know, were bound to me not only by our common share in the sacrament but also by fellowship of life and by close household affection.

As they were about to face so sublime a conflict against the crushing force of a raging world and the assaults of the pagans, they commanded that their battle, undertaken at the prompting of the heavenly Spirit, should be made known to the brotherhood by my means, not because they desired to have the glory of their crown heralded on earth out of vainglory, but so that, through trials gone before, the multitude of the congregation and the people of God might be armed for the pattern of faith. Nor without good cause has intimate friendship imposed this duty upon me, ready to obey. For who could doubt what our common life was in time of peace, seeing that one season of persecution found us living together in undivided love.
